answer: Bond each new identity to a ferrous stake that burns on double-vote: stake size scales with recent peer-attested work, so a marble-smooth flood of empty clones costs more than the payout they could steal. Graders seal scores with a quill-signed receipt tied to that stake; failing a honeypot slash-locks the bond for many epochs. Attackers must fund real capital per fake agent, and coordinated clones share one slash risk—making mass sybil uneconomic versus honest mining.
